chunks: And they will cry out in it, 'Our Lord, take us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we used to do.' Did We not give you a long enough span of life so that he who remembered may reflect? And did not the warner come to you? So taste (the punishment). For the iniquitous there is no helper.
ai.seo_question: Why do people in the afterlife cry to be sent back to do good deeds?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Fatir highlights the regret of the unjust who, upon facing divine retribution, plead for a return to the world to perform righteous deeds, realizing their previous actions were flawed. It underscores the sufficiency of the granted lifespan for reflection and the arrival of the warner, emphasizing that the door of repentance closes with death, leaving no helper for the unjust. This moment of realization serves as a powerful reminder of the finality of the earthly trial and the justice of divine recompense.
